title: Senior's toolkit: pytest, uv and the CI checks
summary: Run exactly the tests you need, debug a failing one, and manage a project with uv the way Python teams do in 2026.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: pytest, uv and the CI checks
steps.body: A working Python project is `uv` for dependencies, `pytest` for tests, and `ruff` plus an audit in CI. These are the flags people type many times a day.

toolkit.what: Choose which tests run, and stop wasting minutes on the rest.
flags: only tests whose names match the expression
rerun only the tests that failed last time

toolkit.what: Run one test by its node id (file, then `::` and the test name). pytest prints these ids for every failure, ready to paste.
flags: one method in a test class

toolkit.what: Understand a failure: more detail, your prints, or the debugger at the failing line.
flags: full diffs of what was expected and what you got
show `print` output instead of capturing it
open the debugger where the test failed

toolkit.what: One test function, many cases. Each case is reported (and can be rerun) on its own.
Built-in fixtures: ask for them as parameters. Each test gets a fresh one, and pytest undoes the changes afterwards.
flags: a new empty folder (a `Path`) for this test
change an environment variable or replace an attribute
what the code printed to stdout and stderr
toolkit.example:
def test_report(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("REPORT_DIR", str(tmp_path))
    write_report()
    assert (tmp_path / "report.txt").exists()

toolkit.what: uv manages the project: `pyproject.toml` lists what you need, `uv.lock` pins exact versions, and both are committed.
flags: uv add httpx / uv add --dev pytest
install exactly the lock; fail if it is out of date (CI)
move one package to its newest allowed version

toolkit.what: The formatter, Black-compatible. In CI, check rather than rewrite, so a badly formatted change fails the build.
flags: exit with an error if any file would change

toolkit.what: Check your installed or pinned dependencies against the database of known vulnerabilities.
flags: audit a requirements file instead of the current environment
fail if any dependency cannot be audited

steps.prompt: The test suite takes 4 minutes and one test, `test_refund_partial`, failed. What do you type to rerun only that test and stop in the debugger where it fails?
options: `pytest -vv` and wait for the whole suite again
steps.explain: `--lf` reruns the tests that failed last time; `-k` selects by name. `--pdb` opens pdb at the failing assert with every local variable available.

steps.prompt: Match each pytest option to what it does.
Test that `write_report()` writes into the folder named by the `REPORT_DIR` environment variable, without touching the real one.
steps.explain: `monkeypatch.setenv` sets the variable for this test only and restores it afterwards. `tmp_path` is a fresh folder, so the assertion cannot pass by accident.

steps.prompt: Put the steps of starting a tested project with uv in order.
Your branch passes locally, but CI fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'httpx'`. You had run `pip install httpx` in your shell. What is the fix?
options: `uv add httpx` so it is in pyproject.toml and uv.lock, commit both, and let CI run `uv sync --locked`
Add `pip install httpx` as the first line of the test file
Ask CI admins to install httpx on the build machines
Pin the CI Python version to yours
steps.explain: `pip install` changed only your environment. Declared, locked dependencies make every machine install the same thing, and `--locked` makes CI fail loudly if the lock file was not updated.

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: While fixing a bug, live in `pytest -k name -x` and `--lf`; run the full suite before you push. Add every dependency with `uv add` and commit `uv.lock`, and make CI run `uv sync --locked`, `ruff format --check`, `ruff check` and your tests, so the pipeline catches what reviewers should not have to.
